Leishman Donovan (LD) bodies Found in untreated leishmaniasis. They are light blue, ellipsoid structures measuring 2-4 μm in length. LD bodies have an eccentric nucleus and a smaller kinetosome at the opposite pole. These bodies are located within large macrophages (also known as Wright's cells).

Dohle bodies Light blue-grey, oval, basophilic staining inclusions were found in the cytoplasm of neutrophils in the peripheral smear. Seen in bacterial infections like tuberculosis, diphtheria, and typhoid, Indicate defective neutrophil production and maturation.

Hendersen Petersen bodies Molluscum contagiosum, caused by a poxvirus, is characterised by the presence of large, ellipsoid intracytoplasmic inclusions in the stratum spinosum and corneum of infected skin known as Henderson-Peterson bodies. They are made up of nuclear and cytoplasmic protein aggregates and mark the site of viral replication.

Councilman Bodies Acidophilic inclusion bodies are found in the cytoplasm of hepatocytes in viral infections like hepatitis and yellow fever. These bodies result from hepatocyte apoptosis and are associated with ballooning degeneration of liver cells. Cowdry Type A bodies Cowdry bodies are eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions made of nucleic acid and protein, seen in infections like herpes, yellow fever, polio, and adenovirus. Type A (found in herpes and yellow fever) appears as droplet-like masses with clear halos and chromatin

Negri bodies Negri bodies are eosinophilic, cytoplasmic inclusion bodies found in neurons, primarily in rabies infection. They represent sites of viral replication and are considered a hallmark of rabies in histopathological examination.
